title: Choose the CodexRouter visual direction
question: The roll assigned the Park Atlas Desk. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Each option keeps your confirmed warm, clear, colorful direction.

options.label: Park Atlas Desk
options.lineage: WPA national park travel posters and field maps
options.thesis: Turn account health and request flow into a field atlas operators can scan in a glance.
options.viewport: A compact left rail frames a warm operations canvas. The first view leads with live Router health, a layered route map for the active account and its quota windows, then a precise request ledger. Every layer corresponds to account, quota, model, or runtime state.
options.risk: The atlas can drift into illustration; every colored plane must carry live operational meaning.

raised.raise: One continuous warm field stock binds navigation, overview, Jev, and activity instead of changing material language by screen.

options.label: Enamel Control Bench
options.thesis: Make account health readable as a set of dependable, color-coded instruments.
options.viewport: A slim vertical nav anchors a broad control bench. Router state owns the lead instrument; quota meters, account switches, recent events, and Jev modes share a measured grid and consistent control geometry.
options.risk: Instrument imagery can add too much chrome if each value receives its own panel.

options.label: Transit Route Board
options.thesis: Show each request as a route through eligible accounts and quota stops.
options.viewport: A rail-style route map leads the overview; eligible accounts become labeled stops and quota or cooldown changes become explicit route states, with a request table below.
options.case: Strong on audience identification and flow clarity; weaker than the atlas across setup, credentials, and Jev policy screens.
options.risk: The metaphor may oversimplify account eligibility and quota rules.

options.label: Phosphor Operations Terminal
options.thesis: Present live traffic as a single searchable operations transcript.
options.viewport: A live request transcript sits beside a compact account and quota rail, with focused filters and a Jev decision trace.
options.case: Clear for event investigation, but less recognizable as a place to manage accounts and model policy.
options.kept: The system makes current status and live events immediately visible.
options.risk: A transcript would dominate tasks that are not log investigation.

options.label: Dawn Cue Desk
options.thesis: Let named runtime phases clarify setup, healthy operation, and recovery.
options.viewport: A labeled runtime timeline distinguishes stopped, ready, active, cooldown, and error states; account and request detail remains in familiar tables.
options.case: State sequencing is clear, but the theater frame adds little to multi-account administration.
options.kept: Named state phases remain visible and never rely on color alone.
options.risk: The lighting metaphor can obscure causal routing details.

options.label: Warm Mission Console
options.thesis: Give each account and routing policy a clear status, owner, and next action.
options.viewport: Account status leads the overview. Setup and Jev policies use a shared panel grammar with unmistakable labels, colored states, and action rows.
options.case: Operational hierarchy is strong, while its fictional lineage is less specific to real Codex account work than the atlas.
options.risk: The console can become costume if stencil labels replace ordinary product language.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar, polished desktop admin console with navigation, summary panels, tables, and conventional forms.
canonCard.viewport: A vertical sidebar frames a live operations overview with account health, request activity, and a conventional settings area; Jev sits in its own nav destination.
canonCard.risk: Familiar patterns make it easy to operate but less distinctive to CodexRouter.
